findings.rationale: From round 11 on, UT's GenHlth distribution moves away from the federation (shift_sd jumps from about 0-0.07 in rounds 1-10 to 0.41-0.71 in rounds 11-20, with GenHlth as the top shifted feature in most of those rounds). The final-round feature screen independently shows UT's GenHlth mean far below the median (z_noise -4.9), so two tools agree on the same feature.

Weaker lead. GA's update norm and cosine change at round 11 (norm ratio rises from about 1 to 2.4 and cosine turns negative), and its drift shift_sd jumps at round 11. Its final-round local performance is also off (CITL -0.057, AUC 0.752). Two tools point to the same onset, but the drift signal is noisier than UT's and the final-round feature screen does not show a GenHlth shift, so confidence is moderate.

report.summary: Budget is fully spent (20.0 epsilon used across screening and confirmation calls). The strongest finding is UT: a clear GenHlth distribution shift from round 11 onward, confirmed by two tools. GA is reported as a moderate-confidence drift lead, because its update anomaly and drift onset both fall at round 11, but its drift signal is noisier. Several other clients showed weaker, noise-level anomalies and are not reported: GU (small n=708, erratic per-round updates, norm flag z=+4.2, which could be explanation_instability or free_rider), WI (post-round-10 GenHlth/HighBP shifts resembling UT's but weaker and less consistent), NC (norm z=-3.4), and several single-statistic feature outliers (GA/UT/WI HighBP, NC HighChol, NM HighChol, DC BMI, PR PhysHlth). None meet the evidence bar for a finding, and no subgroup_bias or missing_artefact pattern with consistent direction emerged. Confidence in GU/WI is low and they would need more budget to resolve.
